Resident.title: Resident
Resident.description: Represents a resident within the condominium.

firstName.description: The first name of the resident.

lastName.description: The last name of the resident.

email.description: The email address of the resident.

phone.description: The phone number of the resident.

unitNumber.description: The unit number of the resident.

Staff.title: Staff
Staff.description: Represents a staff member of the condominium.

id.description: Unique identifier for the staff member.

firstName.description: The first name of the staff member.

lastName.description: The last name of the staff member.

email.description: The email address of the staff member.

phone.description: The phone number of the staff member.

position.description: The job title or position of the staff member.

Vehicle.title: Vehicle
Vehicle.description: Represents a vehicle owned by a resident.

year.description: The year the vehicle was manufactured.

licensePlate.description: The license plate number of the vehicle.

Package.title: Package
Package.description: Represents a package delivered to the condominium.

trackingNumber.description: The tracking number of the package.

carrier.description: The carrier that delivered the package (e.g., USPS, UPS, FedEx).

deliveryDate.description: The date and time the package was delivered.

pickupDate.description: The date and time the package was picked up by the resident.

receivedBy.description: The staff member who received the package. (Reference to Staff if tracking who received it)

CommonArea.title: CommonArea
CommonArea.description: Represents a common area within the condominium that can be booked.

id.description: Unique identifier for the common area.

name.description: The name of the common area (e.g., Gym, Pool, Clubhouse).

description.description: A description of the common area.

capacity.description: The maximum capacity of the common area.

Booking.title: Booking
Booking.description: Represents a booking for a common area.

startTime.description: The start date and time of the booking.

endTime.description: The end date and time of the booking.

status.description: The status of the booking (e.g., Pending, Approved, Cancelled).

Incident.title: Incident
Incident.description: Represents an incident reported by a resident or staff member.

reporterId.description: Reference to Resident or Staff who reported the incident.  (Can determine the table via a prefix or separate fields)

incidentType.description: The type of incident (e.g., Maintenance Request, Complaint, Security Issue).

description.description: A detailed description of the incident.

location.description: The location where the incident occurred.

dateReported.description: The date and time the incident was reported.

status.description: The current status of the incident (e.g., Open, In Progress, Resolved).

startTime.description: The start date and time of the meeting.

endTime.description: The end date and time of the meeting.

attendeeIds.description: References to Residents attending the meeting. (Relationship: Meeting 1:N Resident)

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the TreeCondo application, focusing on security, scalability, and ease of management. The structure leverages path-based ownership for private user data (residents), and membership maps for collaborative data. 

Authorization Independence is achieved by avoiding `get()` calls in security rules. This is accomplished by denormalizing relevant authorization data (e.g., roles, membership lists) directly into the documents that require authorization checks.  For example, while not explicitly collaborative, if 'Staff' require elevated permissions to read/write 'Incidents', denormalizing a `staff_flag: true` into the `Incident` document would eliminate the need to read a staff record during a security check.

The design also supports secure `list` operations by structurally segregating data based on access requirements. For example, resident-owned data is stored under `/residents/{residentId}`, ensuring that listing operations are always scoped to the current user.  The membership map approach allows for controlled access to shared resources like common areas and meetings, allowing authorized users to be efficiently listed.
